Management began identifying these issues during the third quarter of 2026 and initiated corrective actions, including targeted customer outreach, invoice reformatting activities and system process enhancements.

Management estimates that approximately $5.0 million of accounts receivable at September 30, 2026 were attributable to delayed invoicing and collection timing associated with these ERP-related issues.

The Company's collection trends improved throughout the third quarter and into October 2026, and management estimates that approximately $1.3 million of the excess accounts receivable balance had been collected subsequent to quarter end through the date of this filing.

While collection timing remains below historical levels, management believes the underlying receivables are substantially collectible and expects continued improvement in cash collections as reformatting efforts are completed and customer billing processes normalize.
